title: Lime and Cardamom Buttermilk Frozen Yoghurt
changes_from_base: A cooked milk, cream and cream-cheese base thickened with cornflour carries buttermilk, Greek yoghurt, lime syrup and cardamom, instead of plain strained yoghurt.
summary: A sophisticated frozen yoghurt with bright lime juice and aromatic cardamom. Smooth, tangy and beautifully perfumed.

ingredients.item: fresh lime juice (3-4 limes; peel the zest of 3 in wide strips first)

ingredients.note: half with the cream cheese, half in the pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
light corn syrup or glucose syrup

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Simmer 120 ml fresh lime juice with 35 g caster sugar until the sugar dissolves, then cool.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Mix 170 g strained Greek yoghurt and 120 ml buttermilk together; stir 2 tbsp milk with 2 tbsp cornflour to a smooth slurry.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Whisk 57 g cream cheese, half of 130 g caster sugar and ¼ tsp fine salt until smooth, and prepare an ice bath.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: Bring the remaining milk and sugar, 120 ml double cream, 78 g light corn syrup or glucose syrup and the lime zest strips to a rolling boil; simmer for 4 min. Off the heat, whisk in the cornflour slurry and boil again, stirring, for about 1 min until slightly thick.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk the hot custard gradually into the cream cheese mixture, then whisk in the yoghurt mix, lime syrup and ¼ tsp ground cardamom.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Stir the mixture over the ice bath until cold, about 30 min.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Strain into the ice-cream maker and churn until thick.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into a container, press baking paper on the surface, cover and freeze for at least 4 h; keeps for 2 months.

tips: Use fresh lime juice for the best bright flavour; squeeze and strain to remove pulp.
Cool the custard over the ice bath for about 30 min, until completely cold.
This keeps for 2 months, making it perfect for making ahead.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in a sealed freezer container for up to 2 months.
